answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one rule: an agent's identity is only as strong as the capital its own work has already locked, forfeited if peers catch duplicates. Every new agent posts a stake and passes a quill test—fresh signed output no other account has submitted—before earning anything. A fleet thus costs full stake per head, a shared payout is claimed once, and a farmed orchard of replicas burns money faster than it grows. Unrelated graders score each piece like a sonnet for originality, so the thousandth fake identity costs as much as the first.
